draft.title: MLIR calls need activity-specific reverse rules with typed caches
draft.body:
## Reproducer

Run this example

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nsiccha/Enzyme/97121ac5edc086a090bdefd104b79f66b805197a/enzyme/test/MLIR/ReverseMode/custom_rule_sets.mlir -o rule-sets.mlir
enzymemlir-opt rule-sets.mlir --split-input-file --enzyme --canonicalize --lower-enzyme-custom-rules-to-func --remove-unnecessary-enzyme-ops --enzyme-simplify-math --verify-diagnostics | FileCheck rule-sets.mlir
```

## Observed

On the pinned upstream base a callee cannot register the two activity-specific MLIR reverse rules used by the fixture. Its first caller invokes mul(a,x) and mul(3,x) in the same derivative.

## Expected

The first call should differentiate both operands. The second should select the rule for x alone. Each reverse invocation should receive the cached primal values from its own call.

## Proposed fix

Register a set of reverse rules on the callee, select the compatible rule with the fewest active arguments, and lower its saved values to typed call results and operands. See the existing proposals [#2516](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme/pull/2516) and [#3324](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme/pull/3324).
